# QS-CFW-9852-71 Quality specification - axle hub CFW-9852-71 (4140)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-9852-71

Scope
This quality specification applies to the forging, heat treatment acceptance, and final inspection of axle hub CFW-9852-71 manufactured at Plant P1. It defines material acceptance criteria, critical dimensional tolerances, hardness requirements, maximum allowable forging weight for handling and tooling limits, inspection methods, record requirements, and nonconformance handling for production and received forgings. The document is intended for use by process engineers, quality inspectors, production supervisors, and shipping/receiving personnel responsible for CFW-9852-71.

Requirements table
- Part identification: CFW-9852-71 as stamped on routing and inspection records.
- Material: steel specification per internal material control for 4140 forgings.
- Hardness acceptance: The hardness range for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is 34-40 HRC.
- Critical bore tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is ±0.06 mm.
- Maximum forging weight: The maximum forging weight for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is 73.0 kg.
- Surface condition: free of laps, seams, and cold shuts that affect fit or function.
- Feature control: all critical features shall conform to the drawing dimensions and tolerances; refer to manufacturing print for feature identification.

Inspection method
General approach
Inspectors shall perform a sequence of checks from incoming material through final shipment. Inspection combines dimensional verification, hardness testing, visual and NDT where applicable, and weight verification. Records shall document acceptance or disposition.

Incoming material
Verify material certification traceability to the heat number on the mill test report. Confirm alloy and heat treatment class per the purchase order and material control documentation. Record the mill test report reference on inspection documentation.

Dimensional inspection
Use calibrated gauging and measuring instruments appropriate for the feature. For the critical bore, measure at the specified datum, using a bore gauge or coordinate measuring device consistent with the shop procedure. Acceptance criteria for the critical bore follow the requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is ±0.06 mm. Document each measured value on the inspection record and note any out-of-tolerance condition.

Hardness testing
Perform hardness tests on specified locations identified on the drawing. Use a calibrated hardness tester and produce a traceable test block verification record. Acceptance follows the hardness requirement: The hardness range for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is 34-40 HRC. Record each hardness reading and the tester verification block result on the inspection sheet.

Weight verification
Confirm forging weight as part of batch control, and to ensure compliance with handling and tooling limits. Verify that production forgings do not exceed the maximum allowed mass by comparing the measured mass against the requirement: The maximum forging weight for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is 73.0 kg. Record mass measurements on the batch load sheet.

Visual and NDT
Inspect visual condition for defects impacting performance. Where required by the manufacturing print, perform nondestructive examination per the applicable shop procedure and record results on the NDT report.

Sampling and acceptance
Perform inspection at defined points in the flow: incoming, post-forge, post-heat-treatment, and final. Any feature that fails to meet the requirement table shall be documented as nonconforming and processed per the nonconformance handling directive below.

Nonconforming handling
Identification and containment
If an item is found to be nonconforming to any requirement in this document, segregate and tag the item clearly to prevent unintended use. The tag shall reference the inspection record and the reason for rejection.

Disposition
Evaluate nonconforming items to determine whether rework, repair, or scrap is applicable. Rework plans must be approved by the process engineer and must explicitly state the affected features and verification steps post-rework. Repair shall not be performed in a manner that would violate metallurgical or dimensional requirements, including hardness and bore tolerance.

Example dispositions
- A hub with a bore out of tolerance shall be submitted to engineering for a rework evaluation. If a rework method is approved, post-rework inspection must confirm compliance with: The bore diameter tolerance for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is ±0.06 mm.
- A hub with hardness outside the acceptance range shall be held and reviewed by metallurgical engineering. Any heat treatment adjustment must result in confirmation that: The hardness range for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is 34-40 HRC before release.

Records to keep
Maintain an inspection packet for each production lot that includes at minimum:
- Incoming material certification and mill test report reference.
- Dimensional inspection records showing measured values for critical features, including the bore and its conformity to the tolerance: ±0.06 mm.
- Hardness test records with tester verification showing conformity to: 34-40 HRC.
- Mass record demonstrating forgings do not exceed: 73.0 kg where applicable.
- NDT reports and visual inspection notes.
- Nonconformance tags, disposition documentation, and rework approvals.

Retention and access
Inspection records shall be retained in the document control system and made available during internal audits and customer inspections. Each record shall reference the part CFW-9852-71 and the production lot identifier.

Rationale and background
Hardness and bore tolerance are critical to ensuring proper fit, fatigue life, and assembly function for axle hub CFW-9852-71. The specified hardness range provides a balance between wear resistance and toughness for the 4140 material condition typical for this hub. The tight bore tolerance is required to achieve proper interference or clearance fits with mating shafts and bearings. Maximum forging weight is specified to prevent overloading of handling equipment and tooling and to ensure that process controls validated at the specified mass remain valid.

Change control
Any change to these requirements must be approved through the formal document revision process and coordinated with process engineering, production, and quality assurance. This is Revision Rev C for Plant P1 for parts CFW-9852-71.
